title: Chatbots — Rule-Based to Neural to LLM Agents

questions.question: Which response does rule_based_respond("My name is Alex") produce?
options: Nice to meet you, Alex.
Hello. How can I help?
Why do you name Alex?
Tell me more about that.
questions.explanation: The first matching RulePattern captures the name and formats it into the greeting template.

questions.question: Why are the RulePattern entries checked in their listed order?
options: Regex matching always ignores the order of a list
The catch-all .* pattern would otherwise match before more specific patterns
The last pattern is the only one that can capture groups
Order controls the FAQ Jaccard threshold, not rule selection
questions.explanation: rule_based_respond returns on the first match, and the final catch-all would swallow every input if placed first.

questions.question: What similarity does faq_respond use to compare a user question with an FAQ question?
options: Cosine similarity between trained sentence embeddings
Character edit distance divided by sentence length
Jaccard similarity between their lowercase alphabetic token sets
The number of FAQ entries already answered today
questions.explanation: token_set builds sets, and faq_respond scores intersection size divided by union size.

questions.question: Which input does is_destructive("Please cancel my order") identify as destructive?
options: False, because only delete is destructive
True only if the FAQ also matches
False until a neural classifier sees the input
True, because cancel is in danger_words
questions.explanation: is_destructive lowercases the text and checks whether any word in its fixed danger list occurs.

questions.question: Which route does hybrid_respond choose for "what is the weather like"?
options: agent
rule
faq
It raises because weather is not in FAQ
questions.explanation: The message is not destructive and does not reach the FAQ threshold, so the fallback response labels it agent.

questions.question: Why should a destructive request be routed before an LLM answer in this toy hybrid?
options: Rules understand every open-domain question better than a language model
A structured confirmation path can gate actions such as cancel, refund, or transfer
Routing first guarantees the requested transaction already succeeded
It avoids tokenizing the user input entirely
questions.explanation: The code deliberately returns the rule route for danger words, separating action authorization from free-form generation.
